mangan.hint: Recall the score everything else is based on.
mangan.explanation: 5 han is mangan, and a non-dealer ron of mangan is 8,000 points.

haneman.hint: 6 to 7 han is haneman: 1.5 times mangan.
haneman.explanation: 6 han is haneman: 1.5 times the 8,000 points of mangan, or 12,000 points.

baiman.hint: 8 to 10 han is baiman: twice mangan.
baiman.explanation: 8 han is baiman: twice the 8,000 points of mangan, or 16,000 points.

manganKoRon.achievement: You can now give the score of a non-dealer ron of mangan or more from its han.

mangan.hint: A non-dealer mangan ron is 8,000 points. Half of it is what the dealer pays, and half of that again is what each non-dealer pays.
mangan.explanation: Mangan is 8,000 points in total. The dealer pays 4,000 points, and each non-dealer pays 2,000 points.

haneman.hint: A non-dealer haneman ron is 12,000 points. Halve it, then halve it again.
haneman.explanation: Haneman is 12,000 points in total. The dealer pays 6,000 points, and each non-dealer pays 3,000 points.

baiman.hint: A non-dealer baiman ron is 16,000 points.
baiman.explanation: Baiman is 16,000 points in total. The dealer pays 8,000 points, and each non-dealer pays 4,000 points.

manganKoTsumo.achievement: You can now work out the payments for a non-dealer tsumo of mangan or more from the non-dealer ron score.

mangan.hint: A non-dealer mangan is 8,000 points. The dealer gets 1.5 times that.
mangan.explanation: 5 han is mangan, and a dealer ron is 1.5 times the non-dealer's 8,000 points, or 12,000 points.

haneman.hint: A non-dealer haneman is 12,000 points. The dealer gets 1.5 times that.
haneman.explanation: 6 han is haneman, and a dealer ron is 1.5 times the non-dealer's 12,000 points, or 18,000 points.

baiman.hint: Baiman is twice mangan. A dealer mangan is 12,000 points.
baiman.explanation: 8 han is baiman, and a dealer ron is twice the dealer mangan of 12,000 points, or 24,000 points.

manganOyaRon.achievement: You can now give the score of a dealer ron of mangan or more as 1.5 times the non-dealer score.

mangan.hint: A dealer mangan ron is 12,000 points. The three non-dealers split it equally.
mangan.explanation: Mangan is 12,000 points in total. The three non-dealers pay 4,000 points each: “4,000 all”.

haneman.hint: A dealer haneman ron is 18,000 points. Divide it by 3.
haneman.explanation: Haneman is 18,000 points in total. The three non-dealers pay 6,000 points each: “6,000 all”.

baiman.hint: A dealer baiman ron is 24,000 points.
baiman.explanation: Baiman is 24,000 points in total. The three non-dealers pay 8,000 points each: “8,000 all”.

manganOyaTsumo.achievement: You can now work out the payments for a dealer tsumo of mangan or more by dividing the dealer ron score by 3.

riichi.hint: The most basic yaku, and one that only a closed hand can have.
riichi.explanation: Riichi is 1 han. Only a closed hand can have it: once you call, it no longer counts.

toitoiNaki.hint: You build this yaku by collecting triplets with pon, so calling does not lower its han.
toitoiNaki.explanation: Toitoi is 2 han. Its han stay the same when you call.

honitsuMenzen.hint: Check the table for its han with a closed hand.
honitsuMenzen.explanation: Honitsu is 3 han with a closed hand.

honitsuNaki.hint: Honitsu is a kuisagari yaku: calling makes it 1 han less than when closed.
honitsuNaki.explanation: Once you call, honitsu drops 1 han from its closed 3 han to 2 han (kuisagari).

yaku.achievement: You can now count the han of a yaku, including how calling changes them (kuisagari).

jantouFu.questionPrompt: Choose the fu for the pair

sangen.hint: The white, green and red dragons are the dragons. This is a pair of value tiles.
sangen.explanation: The white dragon is a dragon, so as the pair it is 2 fu. A pair of dragons is always 2 fu, whatever the round wind and seat wind are.

jikaze.hint: For the South player, South is your own wind.
jikaze.explanation: For the South player, South is the seat wind, so it is 2 fu. Not only a round wind (East) pair but also a seat wind pair earns fu.

otakaze.hint: For the South player in the East round, West is neither the round wind nor the seat wind.
otakaze.explanation: West is neither the round wind (East) nor the seat wind (South). It is a guest wind, so it is 0 fu. A wind tile does not always earn fu.

suuhai.hint: Check the summary table to see whether a pair of number tiles earns fu.
suuhai.explanation: 5 pin is a number tile, so it is 0 fu. A pair of number tiles never earns fu.

jantouFu.achievement: You can now tell the pairs that earn fu (dragons, the round wind, your seat wind) from those that do not (number tiles, guest winds).

mentsuFu.questionPrompt: Choose the fu for the set

minkouSimple.hint: One tile turned sideways marks a call. An open triplet of simples is the starting value for triplet fu.
minkouSimple.explanation: This is an open triplet of simples, made by calling pon on 5 man, so it is 2 fu. From here, being closed, being terminals or honors and being a quad each double the fu.

ankouYaochu.hint: No tile is turned sideways, so it is a closed triplet, and 9 is a terminal. Being closed doubles the fu, and being a terminal doubles them again.
ankouYaochu.explanation: A closed triplet of 9 sou is a closed triplet of terminals, so the 2 fu of an open triplet doubles and doubles again to 8 fu.

minkanSimple.hint: A quad is worth 4 times a triplet of the same kind of tile, open or closed in the same way. An open triplet of simples is 2 fu.
minkanSimple.explanation: An open quad of 5 sou is an open quad of simples, so it is 4 times the 2 fu of an open triplet of simples: 8 fu.

ankanYaochu.hint: Both end tiles face down, so it is a closed quad. The red dragon is an honor tile, so it counts as terminals and honors. A closed triplet of terminals or honors is 8 fu.
ankanYaochu.explanation: A closed quad of red dragons is a closed quad of honors, so it is 4 times the 8 fu of a closed triplet of terminals or honors: 32 fu. That is the most fu a set can earn.

mentsuFu.achievement: You can now work out the fu for triplets and quads from whether they are open or closed and the kind of tile (simples, or terminals and honors).

machiFu.questionPrompt: Choose the fu for the wait

ryanmen.hint: A shape that wins on a tile on either side of 3 and 4 (2 or 5).
ryanmen.explanation: 3 pin and 4 pin waiting on 2 pin or 5 pin is a two-sided wait, so it is 0 fu. A wait that accepts many tiles earns no fu.

kanchan.hint: A shape that waits only on the one tile between 4 and 6.
kanchan.explanation: 4 man and 6 man waiting only on 5 man is a closed wait, so it is 2 fu.

penchan.hint: A shape at the end, 8 and 9, that waits only on the 7 on one side.
penchan.explanation: 8 sou and 9 sou waiting only on 7 sou is an edge wait, so it is 2 fu. Like 1 and 2 waiting on 3, it can only accept a tile on one side.

shanpon.hint: A shape that wins when either of two pairs becomes a triplet.
shanpon.explanation: A pair of 2 man and a pair of West, waiting on either one, is a pair wait, so it is 0 fu.

tanki.hint: A shape that holds a single tile and waits on the same tile.
tanki.explanation: A single 7 pin waiting on 7 pin is a single-tile wait, so it is 2 fu.

machiFu.achievement: You can now look at a tenpai shape and tell whether its wait earns fu (closed, edge and single-tile waits are 2 fu; two-sided and pair waits are 0 fu).

tehaiFu.condition: {bakaze} round, {jikaze} seat, win by {winType, select, tsumo {tsumo} other {ron}}
tehaiFu.questionPrompt: Choose the fu for the whole hand

furoRon.hint: A ron with called sets gets neither the closed ron bonus nor tsumo fu. Add the open triplet of white dragons and the wait, then round up at the end.
furoRon.explanation: 20 base fu + 4 fu for the open triplet of white dragons + 2 fu for the closed wait = 26 fu, rounded up to 30 fu. It is a ron with called sets, so nothing is added for how you won.

furoTsumo.hint: Even with called sets, a tsumo win gets tsumo fu.
furoTsumo.explanation: 20 base fu + 2 tsumo fu + 4 fu for the open triplet of white dragons + 4 fu for the closed triplet of 8 pin + 2 fu for the closed wait = 32 fu, rounded up to 40 fu. Forget the tsumo fu and you get 30 fu.

shanponRon.hint: When you win by ron on a pair wait, the triplet that contains the ron tile counts as an open triplet.
shanponRon.explanation: 20 base fu + 10 fu closed ron bonus + 8 fu each for the closed triplets of 9 man and 1 pin + 4 fu for the open triplet of white dragons completed by the ron = 50 fu. Count the white dragons as a closed triplet and you get 54 fu, which rounds up to 60 fu.

nanBakaze.hint: In the South round, the round wind is South.
nanBakaze.explanation: 20 base fu + 2 tsumo fu + 8 fu for the closed triplet of 9 man + 2 fu for the pair of South (round wind) = 32 fu, rounded up to 40 fu. Mistake East for the round wind and you get 30 fu.

tehaiFu.achievement: You can now work out the fu for a whole hand by adding the base fu, the fu for how you won, the sets, the pair and the wait, then rounding up.

chiitoitsuScore.condition: {role, select, oya {Dealer} other {Non-dealer}}, {winType, select, tsumo {tsumo} other {ron}}, {yaku} ({han} han)

only.hint: Chiitoitsu is 25 fu by tsumo or by ron. Look up a non-dealer ron at 25 fu 2 han in the table.
only.explanation: Chiitoitsu is 25 fu. A non-dealer ron at 25 fu 2 han is 1,600 points.

tanyao.hint: When other yaku are added, the fu stay at 25. Only the han change.
tanyao.explanation: With tanyao added it is 3 han, and the fu stay at 25. A non-dealer ron at 25 fu 3 han is 3,200 points.

riichiTanyao.hint: The fu stay at 25, and it is 4 han: the right end of the non-dealer table.
riichiTanyao.explanation: With riichi and tanyao added it is 4 han, and the fu stay at 25. A non-dealer ron at 25 fu 4 han is 6,400 points.

oyaRiichi.hint: The dealer table uses the same 25 fu. Look up a dealer ron at 3 han.
oyaRiichi.explanation: With riichi added it is 3 han, at 25 fu. A dealer ron at 25 fu 3 han is 4,800 points.

chiitoitsuScore.achievement: You can now use the fixed 25 fu of chiitoitsu to look up the score in the table when other yaku are added.

pinfuScore.condition: {role, select, oya {Dealer} other {Non-dealer}}, {winType, select, tsumo {tsumo} other {ron}}, {yaku} ({han} han)
pinfuScore.questionPrompt: Choose the score (for a tsumo, the non-dealer / dealer payments)

ron.hint: A pinfu ron is 30 fu. Look up a non-dealer ron at 30 fu 1 han in the table.
ron.explanation: A pinfu ron gets the closed ron bonus and is 30 fu. A non-dealer ron at 30 fu 1 han is 1,000 points.

tsumo.hint: A pinfu tsumo is 20 fu. Look up the tsumo payments in the tsumo row of the table (non-dealer / dealer).
tsumo.explanation: A pinfu tsumo is 20 fu, and with menzen tsumo added it is 2 han. On a non-dealer tsumo at 20 fu 2 han, each non-dealer pays 400 points and the dealer pays 700 points.

tanyaoRon.hint: Even with tanyao added, a ron stays at 30 fu.
tanyaoRon.explanation: With tanyao added it is 2 han, and the fu stay at 30. A non-dealer ron at 30 fu 2 han is 2,000 points.

tanyaoTsumo.hint: Even with tanyao added, a tsumo stays at 20 fu.
tanyaoTsumo.explanation: With menzen tsumo and tanyao added it is 3 han, and the fu stay at 20. On a non-dealer tsumo at 20 fu 3 han, each non-dealer pays 700 points and the dealer pays 1,300 points.

pinfuScore.achievement: You can now use the fixed fu of pinfu (20 fu by tsumo, 30 fu by ron) to look up the score in the table when other yaku are added.

menzenMentsuScore.condition: {handShape, select, furo {Open} other {Closed}}, {winType, select, tsumo {tsumo} other {ron}}, built-up fu: {extraFu} fu
menzenMentsuScore.questionPrompt: Choose the fu for the hand

ron2.hint: Add the 20 base fu, the 10 fu closed ron bonus and the built-up fu, then round up to the next 10 fu.
ron2.explanation: 20 + 10 + 2 = 32 fu, which rounds up (tenpane) to 40 fu. A closed ron that is not pinfu always has some fu built up, so it is 40 fu or more.

tsumo8.hint: Add the 20 base fu, the 2 fu for tsumo and the built-up fu, then round up to the next 10 fu.
tsumo8.explanation: 20 + 2 + 8 = 30 fu. It is an exact multiple of 10, so it does not round up and stays at 30 fu (for example, a hand whose only fu come from one closed triplet of terminals or honors).

tsumo10.hint: Do not forget to add the 2 fu for tsumo.
tsumo10.explanation: 20 + 2 + 10 = 32 fu, which rounds up to 40 fu. By ron it would be exactly 20 + 10 + 10 = 40 fu, so it comes to the same 40 fu.

ron12.hint: Add the 10 fu closed ron bonus, then round up.
ron12.explanation: 20 + 10 + 12 = 42 fu, which rounds up to 50 fu. With the same 12 fu, a tsumo would be 20 + 2 + 12 = 34 fu and round up to 40 fu, so the ron comes out 10 fu higher.

menzenMentsuScore.achievement: You can now work out the fu for a closed hand that is not pinfu by adding the base fu, the fu for tsumo or ron and the built-up fu and rounding up, and you can tell where the total rounds up.

furoScore.condition: {handShape, select, furo {Open} other {Closed}}, {winType, select, tsumo {tsumo} other {ron}}, built-up fu: {extraFu} fu
furoScore.questionPrompt: Choose the fu for the hand

ron4.hint: A ron with an open hand gets no closed ron bonus. Add the built-up fu to the 20 base fu, then round up to the next 10 fu.
ron4.explanation: 20 + 4 = 24 fu, which rounds up (tenpane) to 30 fu. Closed, it would be 20 + 10 + 4 = 34 fu and 40 fu, so calling makes a ron 10 fu lower.

ron0.hint: A ron with 0 built-up fu is the exception (the open pinfu shape).
ron0.explanation: A ron with 0 built-up fu totals 20 fu, but 20 fu is reserved for a pinfu tsumo, so it is treated as 30 fu (the open pinfu shape).

tsumo10.hint: Tsumo fu are the same as for a closed hand. Add the 20 base fu, the 2 fu for tsumo and the built-up fu, then round up.
tsumo10.explanation: 20 + 2 + 10 = 32 fu, which rounds up to 40 fu. The 2 fu for tsumo still apply with an open hand.

ron10.hint: A ron starts from the 20 base fu alone.
ron10.explanation: 20 + 10 = 30 fu. It is an exact multiple of 10, so it does not round up and stays at 30 fu. With the same 10 fu, a tsumo would be 32 fu and round up to 40 fu, so with an open hand the tsumo comes out higher.

furoScore.achievement: You can now work out the fu for an open hand by adding up from the 20 base fu for a ron, or from 22 fu for a tsumo as with a closed hand, then rounding up (the open pinfu shape is 30 fu).
